entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 28 Job 28:1-28 . Job's Speech Continued. In the twenty-seventh chapter Job had tacitly admitted that the statement of the friends was often true, that God vindicated His justice by punishing the wicked here; but still the affliction of the godly remained unexplained. Man has, by skill, brought the precious metals from their concealment. But the Divine Wisdom, which governs human affairs, he cannot similarly discover ( Job 28:12 , &c.). However, the image from the same metals ( Job 23:10 ) implies Job has made some way towards solving the riddle of his life; namely, that affliction is to him as the refining fire is to gold. 1. vein-- a mine, from which it goes forth, Hebrew, "is dug." place for gold-- a place where gold may be found, which men refine. Not as English Version, "A place--where," (Mal 3:3). Contrasted with gold found in the bed and sand of rivers, which does not need refining; as the gold dug from a mine does. Golden ornaments have been found in Egypt, of the times of Joseph.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5044"/><div sID="gen7472" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5044"/>4. Three hardships in mining: 1. "A stream (flood) breaks out at the side of the stranger"; namely, the miner, a strange newcomer into places heretofore unexplored; his surprise at the sudden stream breaking out beside him is expressed (English Version, "from the inhabitant"). 2. "Forgotten (unsupported) by the foot they hang," namely, by ropes, in descending. In the Hebrew, "Lo there" precedes this clause, graphically placing it as if before the eyes. "The waters" is inserted by English Version. "Are dried up," ought to be, "hang," "are suspended." English Version perhaps understood, waters of whose existence man was previously unconscious, and near which he never trod; and yet man's energy is such, that by pumps, &c., he soon causes them to "dry up and go away" [So Herder]. 3. "Far away from men, they move with uncertain step"; they stagger; not "they are gone" [Umbreit]. <div eID="gen7472" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5045"/><div sID="gen7473" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5045"/>5. Its fertile surface yields food; and yet "beneath it is turned up as it were with fire." So Pliny [Natural History, 33] observes on the ingratitude of man who repays the debt he owes the earth for food, by digging out its bowels. "Fire" was used in mining [Umbreit]. English Version is simpler, which means precious stones which glow like fire; and so <reference osisRef="Job.28.6">Job 28:6</reference> follows naturally (<reference osisRef="Ezek.28.14">Eze 28:14</reference>). <div eID="gen7473" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5046"/><div sID="gen7474" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5046"/>6. Sapphires are found in alluvial soil near rocks and embedded in gneiss. The ancients distinguished two kinds: 1. The real, of transparent blue: 2. That improperly so called, opaque, with gold spots; that is, lapis lazuli. To the latter, looking like gold dust, Umbreit refers "dust of gold." English Version better, "The stones of the earth are, &c., and the clods of it (Vulgate) are gold"; the parallel clauses are thus neater. <div eID="gen7474" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5052"/><div sID="gen7482" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5052"/>12. Can man discover the Divine Wisdom by which the world is governed, as he can the treasures hidden in the earth? Certainly not. Divine Wisdom is conceived as a person (<reference osisRef="Job.28.12-Job.28.27">Job 28:12-27</reference>) distinct from God (<reference osisRef="Job.28.23">Job 28:23</reference>; also in <reference osisRef="Prov.8.23">Pr 8:23</reference>, <reference osisRef="Prov.8.27">27</reference>). The Almighty Word, Jesus Christ, we know now, is that Wisdom. The order of the world was originated and is maintained by the breathing forth (Spirit) of Wisdom, unfathomable and unpurchasable by man. In <reference osisRef="Job.28.28">Job 28:28</reference>, the only aspect of it, which relates to, and may be understood by, man, is stated.<div eID="gen7482" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7483" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">understanding--</hi>insight into the plan of the divine government. <div eID="gen7483" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5060"/><div sID="gen7496" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5060"/>21. None can tell whence or where, seeing it, &c.<div eID="gen7496" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7497" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">fowls--</hi>The gift of divination was assigned by the heathen especially to birds. Their rapid flight heavenwards and keen sight originated the superstition. Job may allude to it. Not even the boasted divination of birds has an insight into it (<reference osisRef="Eccl.10.20">Ec 10:20</reference>). But it may merely mean, as in <reference osisRef="Job.28.7">Job 28:7</reference>, It escapes the eye of the most keen-sighted bird. <div eID="gen7497" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_plain: 27. declare-- manifest her, namely, in His works ( Psa 19:1 , 2). So the approval bestowed by the Creator on His works ( Ge 1:10 , 31 ); compare the "rejoicing" of wisdom at the same ( Pr 8:30 ; which Umbreit translates; "I was the skilful artificer by His side"). prepared-- not created, for wisdom is from everlasting ( Pr 8:22-31 ); but "established" her as Governor of the world. searched ... out-- examined her works to see whether she was adequate to the task of governing the world [Maurer].

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5067"/><div sID="gen7508" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5067"/>28. Rather, "But unto man," &c. My wisdom is that whereby all things are governed; Thy wisdom is in fearing God and shunning evil, and in feeling assured that My wisdom always acts aright, though thou dost not understand the principle which regulates it; for example, in afflicting the godly (<reference osisRef="John.7.17">Joh 7:17</reference>). The friends, therefore, as not comprehending the Divine Wisdom, should not infer Job's guilt from his sufferings. Here alone in Job the name of God, Adonai, occurs; "Lord" or "master," often applied to Messiah in Old Testament. Appropriately here, in speaking of the Word or Wisdom, by whom the world was made (<reference osisRef="Prov.8.22-Prov.8.31">Pr 8:22-31</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.1.3">Joh 1:3</reference>; Ecclesiasticus 24:1-34). <chapter eID="Job.28"/>
